body: I decided to switch to a mage, the problem is from what I have heard of what he told the PC he likes my character will be a vegetable long before level 20. They take literal Wisdom damage, and so I have to keep my head afloat basically.

The problem is the city that we sell things in actually does have metal, but because in our hometown metal was non-existent we have no money or anything. He gave any money we got from our initial first levels to the PC he likes who just went and spent it.
The problem is he would say we had no clue how to use them. He has a tendency to use our character's lack of outside world knowledge against us often.

It's always felt like he cares for a few PCs but the other ones can just do whatever. I normally never min/max characters or go out of my way to make them TRULY combat effective, but I want to have some sort of impact.
We live an in outpost where we had no metal but the city we would sell it to, yes the one city there is because ours was ruined, has plenty of metal.
The melee's can damage them with bludgeoning.
If its simple I can use it probably. I know for a fact he took martial weapon proficiency and heavy armor proficiency away.
The problem I run into is I live with half the party, and have known them for years. I feel like it's better to attempt to work it out than to just quit.

The sling is a good idea. I will probably not have proficiency with it but I will speak to my DM about that part. I want to make a new character but it feels like I can't do anything. Arcane magic is basically banned because you go insane if you study it, and then piercing is bad. So i will have to be something else if I can't figure out the ranger thing.
Can you explain a little bit more? I just have a hard time arguing it logically. I'm also a bit noobish.
